The SCOP 1.75 record for 1acc chain A was one whole-chain domain. SCOPe 2.08 splits that chain into two domains in different classes. Details below.

**What changed between releases**

| Release | Domain | Region | Classification |
|---|---|---|---|
| SCOP 1.75 | d1acca_ (sunid 43828) | all of chain A | f.11.1.1, fold f.11 "Anthrax protective antigen", class f |
| SCOPe 2.08 | d1acca2 (sunid 238522) | A:14-225 | b.179.1.1 "PA14", superfamily b.179.1 "PA14-like", fold b.179, class b (all-beta) |
| SCOPe 2.08 | d1acca1 (sunid 238521) | A:226-735 | f.60.1.1 "Anthrax protective antigen C-terminal-like", fold f.60, class f |

The 1.75 fold f.11 was retired. Its contents were re-expressed as two new folds with fresh sunids (254103 for f.60, 254104 for b.179), so the identifiers do not carry over. Both 2.08 domains still carry the "complexed with ca" comment and the species node for Bacillus anthracis. The chain maps to UniProt P13423, and its sequence cluster representative in 2.08 is chain 3tewA, not 1accA itself.

**What the split reveals about domains as evolutionary modules**

The N-terminal region was a protein-specific, single-member unit in 1.75. In 2.08 it is recognized as a PA14 domain, a module that recurs in otherwise unrelated proteins. The PA14 family in 2.08 contains a protein node for a yeast beta-glucosidase PA14 domain from Kluyveromyces marxianus (sunid 254417), alongside the anthrax protein. The family placement asserts a homologous relationship at the family level between these domains, even though the full-length proteins have different functions and different partner domains. A whole-chain domain definition hid this. Treating the chain as one unit conflated two segments with separate evolutionary histories, so the 1.75 fold f.11 was effectively an artifact of under-splitting rather than a real single fold.

The C-terminal region remained a class f unit but is now its own fold, superfamily, and family. In 2.08 it is still a single-protein lineage, so no homology beyond the protein itself is asserted there.

**How this should affect homology searches**

- Search domain-wise, not chain-wise. Use d1acca2 and d1acca1 as separate queries or templates. A whole-chain query mixes two unrelated evolutionary signals and will produce partial hits that are hard to interpret.
- Hits to the PA14 domain imply homology only to the N-terminal module. They do not imply any relationship to the C-terminal region, and they do not justify transferring the anthrax protein's function to a glycosidase or adhesin that carries PA14.
- Family-level membership in b.179.1.1 is the evolutionarily strong claim. Superfamily b.179.1 is also a homology assertion. Fold b.179 alone would not be, and shared fold with any other all-beta domain is not evidence of common ancestry.
- The C-terminal domain's classification in f.60.1.1 gives you only a within-protein family. Finding homologs there requires external evidence such as profile or structural searches against other databases. SCOPe 2.08 does not supply those relatives.
- Pin the release. Older ASTRAL subsets built on 1.75 use d1acca_ and f.11, so results from those sets are not comparable to 2.08-based results without remapping.
- Representative caveat. Chain 3tewA is the sequence-cluster representative for 1accA. Any stored hits for that representative are evidence for the representative, not an official classification of 1acc.
